title: ClickHouse health: replica lag, disk usage, queue depth
description: The rich healthcheck the nexus-cli health verb will surface: per-replica absolute_delay (lag), free disk on the data path, and the replication queue depth. Run over SSH until the ClickHouseAdapter lands.

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.44 "clickhouse-client --secure --host localhost --port 9440 --query 'SELECT database, table, absolute_delay, queue_size, inserts_in_queue, merges_in_queue FROM system.replicas FORMAT PrettyCompact'"

observe.what: absolute_delay ~0s (replicas caught up); queue_size small -- no replication backlog

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.44 "clickhouse-client --secure --host localhost --port 9440 --query 'SELECT name, formatReadableSize(free_space) AS free, formatReadableSize(total_space) AS total FROM system.disks FORMAT PrettyCompact'"

observe.what: free_space on the data disk healthy (lab data volumes are tiny vs the 300 GB VMDK)

whatProves: health surfaces replica lag + disk headroom + queue depth from system.replicas / system.disks -- the operational health signals the ClickHouseAdapter health verb reports.
